subject: colext with correlated covariates for psi/gamma/epsilon

messages.author: 4b155d4db9fdbece
messages.subject: colext with correlated covariates for psi/gamma/epsilon
parts:
Hello all,

Is there a problem with using the same covariate (or highly correlated covariates) in both psi and gamma/epsilon?

Part of me says no because they are separate regression equations. However, at the same time, a model with the same covariate in both psi and gamma/epsilon seems funny to me.

For example, let's say you have a (static) site-covariate "A" and a dynamic site-covariate "B". Let's also say "A" and "B" are highly correlated. Now for a model with psi(A), gamma(B), epsilon(B), one might get the following result: 
  • psi is positively associated with "A"
  • gamma is positively associated with "B"
  • epsilon is negatively associated with "B"
That doesn't seem right to me. I interpret this as meaning "A" is really important and "B" shows up because of the correlation. Or vice-versa of course.

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: colext with correlated covariates for psi/gamma/epsilon
parts:
Hi Matt,

I'm not sure parameter estimation is an issue: these are regressions for z_1 being 0 or 1, and the probabilities of transitioning from occupied to unoccupied and vice versa. A very small value of what has been called P* (a cumulative probability of detecting a present organism at least during one sampling interval) poses problems, but not problems unique to having a shared covariate for each parameter. If you are using some great covariate C that more or less encapsulates the niche, and you start a study with a species being more or less in equilibrium with the environment, and there's no dispersal limitation or anything like that, then a model where C is positively associated with psi and gamma and negatively associated with epsilon could be be completely reasonable. Strong support for modeling psi and dynamics with different predictors can be an indication that the psi predictors are not great habitat descriptors.

Re. your A and B description above, A might be really important and B might be a free-rider, and if so, psi~A, gam~A, eps~A should provide better fit than psi~A, gam~B, eps~B. The predictors for gamma and epsilon don't have to be dynamic.

John
